prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the open 3D geometry of a wide urban street intersection, showing a continuous ground plane gradient from roughly 1 m at the bottom edge out to multi-storey corner buildings 20–50 m away across the five frames as the camera wearer pans right (frames 1–3), left (frame 4), and right again (frame 5). In frame 1, the bright white silhouette in the lower-left foreground places the pink-haired companion's head within arm's reach at roughly 0.5–0.8 m, while in frame 4 her slightly dimmer silhouette at the left edge shows she is now 1.5–2 m away (just beyond arm's reach) with a dark car 5–8 m behind her, and in frame 5 the camera wearer's own raised thumb and held object appear at the bottom-left at about 0.3–0.4 m. Mid-range vehicles—such as the blue SUV ~12–15 m to the right in frame 2 and the receding car ~18–20 m ahead in frame 3—appear as distinct medium-grey shapes against darker background structures and overhead traffic light gantries 15–35 m above the street. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the metric separation between foreground body parts (under 2 m) and background buildings or cars immediately obvious, and clearly outlines the overhead traffic signal poles against the sky. However, the map is unreliable in Frame 3 where looking down at the crosswalk causes the entire near road surface to saturate to pure white, and at distances beyond 25–30 m where cars, trees, and building facades flatten into nearly uniform dark grey values.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete street-scene objects—people, cars, and overhead traffic lights—against a black background across the intersection as the camera wearer turns their head right, left, and right. It tracks the nearby pink-haired companion as a large pink `person` mask cropped at the lower-left in frame 1 (~0.5–0.8 m away, facing right away from the camera wearer, within arm's reach) and standing on the left in frame 4 (~1.5–2 m away, facing right while looking toward the camera wearer), where her mask partially occludes a brown `car` mask 4–6 m directly behind her. In the mid-to-far range, the map labels the blue SUV on the right in frame 2 (~12–15 m away) and the receding blue car in frame 3 (~18–20 m ahead) with cyan `car` masks, alongside smaller `car` masks 25–50 m away, tiny `person` masks ~20–30 m away near the crosswalk corners in frames 2 and 3, and elevated `traffic light` masks hanging 5–6 m above the road at 20–35 m distance. This map highlights tiny distant vehicles, far-off pedestrians, and small overhead traffic signals that are difficult to spot quickly in the wide-angle RGB frames. However, the segmentation is unreliable inseveral places: in frame 5 it completely misses the camera wearer's own hand and held device in the lower foreground (~0.3–0.4 m), in frame 3 it misses the white SUV on the far right (~25 m) and mislabels a red fire hydrant on the central curb (~15 m) as a `person`, and it leaves out all static scene layout such as crosswalks, roads, and buildings.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank (solid black) across all five frames, failing to render any yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons despite the presence of people and hands in the RGB strip. In the RGB context, the pink-haired companion is present in frame 1 at ~0.5–0.8 m on the lower left (within arm's reach, heavily cropped so only her head and sunglasses are visible, facing right) and in frame 4 at ~1.5–2 m on the left (upper body visible, torso angled right while her head turns to look toward the camera wearer, with her left hand raised near her face mask within her own arm's reach). Additionally, in frame 5 the camera wearer's own left thumb and fingers holding an object are visible at the bottom-left edge at ~0.3–0.4 m (within arm's reach), and distant pedestrians stand ~20–30 m away on the far sidewalk in frames 2 and 3. Because the estimator detects nothing, the pose map provides zero spatial information that is hard to see in the RGB images and cannot independently convey body orientation, gaze direction, or reach envelopes. It is entirely unreliable in this sequence due to severe truncation at the frame borders (only a head in frame 1 and a partial hand in frame 5), dark clothing and self-occlusion in frame 4, and the small pixel scale of distant pedestrians.
